Signalling question (PROBAST+AI): Were appropriate data sources used?
How this study meets it (decisions): National Adult Cardiac Surgery Audit (NACSA) registry: prospectively collected national data on every isolated CABG operation in the UK; the study's data extract and its governance are described in the methods (decisions 54 and 94)

Signalling question (PROBAST+AI): Was an appropriate study design used?
How this study meets it (decisions): Registry cohort; development on 2012-16 operations and temporal evaluation on 2017-19 operations (decision 25)

Signalling question (PROBAST+AI): Did the inclusions and exclusions of study participants result in a representative dataset?
How this study meets it (decisions): All isolated CABG operations 2012-16; in-hospital deaths and patients with unknown discharge status or stay excluded by the outcome definition (primary outcome among patients discharged alive; decision 1); composite and all-patient outcomes in sensitivity analyses S1-S2 (decision 99); flow and counts in Figure 1 and ST20

Signalling question (PROBAST+AI): Were predictors defined and assessed in a similar way for all participants?
How this study meets it (decisions): NICOR national data definitions; predictors with definitions that changed over time or fields introduced late were excluded (Step 3 cleaning; ST3-ST4); between-hospital recording differences cannot be checked (no hospital identifier)

Signalling question (PROBAST+AI): Was any preprocessing of predictors similar for all participants?
How this study meets it (decisions): One pipeline (imputation; category coding; splines; scaling) fitted on training patients and applied unchanged to all others (decisions 84 and 101)

Signalling question (PROBAST+AI): Were predictor assessments made without knowledge of outcome data?
How this study meets it (decisions): Predictors are recorded at or before each prediction moment; the outcome (length of stay) is only known at discharge

Signalling question (PROBAST+AI): Were the predictors included in the model available at the time the model was intended to be used?
How this study meets it (decisions): Stage-specific predictor sets defined by when information becomes known (pre-operative; intra-operative, at the end of surgery; early post-operative) (decisions 51 and 57-68); the complication-aware model is labelled as a ceiling analysis not usable in practice (decision 90)

Signalling question (PROBAST+AI): Were outcomes defined and assessed appropriately?
How this study meets it (decisions): Post-operative stay over 10 whole days among patients discharged alive (decision 1); cut-offs of 7 and 14 days in sensitivity analyses S3-S4 (decision 99)

Signalling question (PROBAST+AI): Were outcomes defined and assessed in a similar way for all participants?
How this study meets it (decisions): Same registry field and derivation for every patient (Step 3 rules O1-O4; ST3)

Signalling question (PROBAST+AI): Were outcome assessments made without use or knowledge of predictor data?
How this study meets it (decisions): Length of stay is an administrative date difference not determined from predictors

Signalling question (PROBAST+AI): Was the time interval between predictor assessment and outcome assessment appropriate?
How this study meets it (decisions): Outcome assessed at discharge for every patient; no censoring among patients discharged alive

Signalling question (PROBAST+AI): Was there evidence that the sample size was reasonable?
How this study meets it (decisions): Formal calculation (Riley et al. 2020): available patients are at least 9.7 times the required minimum at every stage (ST7; decision 73)

Signalling question (PROBAST+AI): Were continuous and categorical predictors handled appropriately?
How this study meets it (decisions): No dichotomisation; restricted cubic splines in regression; categories with clinical reference levels (decisions 29 and 101)

Signalling question (PROBAST+AI): Were participants with missing or censored data handled appropriately in the analysis?
How this study meets it (decisions): Stage-ordered chained-equation imputation fitted inside every training set without the outcome (decisions 77-85); multiple imputation (S5) and complete cases (S6) as sensitivity analyses (decisions 74 and 78)

How this study meets it (decisions): No resampling or reweighting for class imbalance was used
